The amount of the regulatory asset is capped at </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">$25.6</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;million.  In December 2013, Cleco Power deferred </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">$8.5</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;million as a regulatory asset.  Amortization of the regulatory asset will commence subsequent to a rate proceeding authorizing such collection.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Condensed Black,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Condensed Black,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">AFUDC Equity Gross-Up</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">Cleco Power capitalizes equity AFUDC as a cost component of construction projects in accordance with the authoritative guidance for regulated operations.  Cleco Power has recorded a regulatory asset to recover the tax gross-up related to the equity component of AFUDC.  These costs are being amortized over the estimated lives of the respective assets constructed.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Condensed Black,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Rate Case Costs</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">In September 2009, the LPSC approved Cleco Power&#8217;s request to recover costs incurred as a result of Cleco Power&#8217;s rate case filed in July 2008.  The new rates became effective upon the commercial operation of Madison Unit 3 on February 12, 2010, and Cleco Power began amortizing the regulatory asset over a </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">four</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">-year period.  </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Condensed Black,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Condensed Black,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Acadia Unit 1 Acquisition Costs</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">In October 2009, the LPSC approved Cleco Power&#8217;s request to establish a regulatory asset for costs incurred as a result of the acquisition by Cleco Power of Acadia Unit 1 and half of Acadia Power Station&#8217;s related common facilities.  Recovery of these expenditures was requested in Cleco Power&#8217;s base rate application filed in July 2008, and these expenditures were covered by the retail rate plan which was approved by the LPSC in October 2009.  The new rates became effective upon the commencement of commercial operation of Madison Unit 3 and Cleco Power began amortizing the regulatory asset over a </font></div></div><div id='pagebreak' style='width:2%; float:left;'>&nbsp;</div><div style='float:right; width:49%;'><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">30</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">-year period.  For more information regarding the Acadia Unit 1 transaction, see Note 18 &#8212; &#8220;Acadia Transactions &#8212; Acadia Unit 1.&#8221;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Condensed Black,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">IRP/RFP Costs </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">In October 2009, the LPSC approved Cleco Power&#8217;s request to establish a regulatory asset to recover IRP and RFP costs incurred.  The new rates became effective upon the commencement of commercial operation of Madison Unit 3 and Cleco Power began amortizing the regulatory asset over a three-year period.  </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Condensed Black,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">AMI Pilot Costs </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">In September 2009, the LPSC approved Cleco Power&#8217;s request to establish a regulatory asset to recover AMI pilot costs incurred.  Recovery of these expenditures was approved by the LPSC in October 2009.  The new rates became effective upon the commercial operation of Madison Unit 3.  In March 2010, Cleco Power began amortizing these costs over a three-year period.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Condensed Black,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Financing Costs</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">In 2011, Cleco Power entered into and settled two treasury rate locks.  Also in 2011, Cleco Power entered into a forward starting swap contract.  These derivatives were entered into in order to mitigate the interest rate exposure on coupon payments related to forecasted debt issuances.  In May 2013, the forward starting interest rate swap was settled at a loss of </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">$3.3 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">.  Cleco Power deferred </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">$2.9 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;of the losses as a regulatory asset.  Cleco Power is amortizing the regulatory asset over the terms of the related debt issuances.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Condensed Black,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Biomass Costs </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">In November 2011, the LPSC approved Cleco Power&#8217;s request to establish a regulatory asset for the non-fuel, non-capital portion of costs incurred to conduct a test burn of biomass fuel at Madison Unit 3.  In August 2012, Cleco Power began amortizing these costs over a </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">five</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">-year period.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Condensed Black,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Fuel and Purchased Power</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">The cost of fuel used for electric generation and the cost of power purchased for utility customers are recovered through the LPSC-established FAC, which enables Cleco Power to pass on to its customers substantially all such charges.  For </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">2013</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, approximately </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">88%</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;of Cleco Power&#8217;s total fuel cost was regulated by the LPSC, while the remainder was regulated by FERC.  </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">The </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$11.7 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;change in the under/over-recovered costs was primarily due to </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$8.6 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;in net mark-to-market gains on open FTR positions and a </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$3.1 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">decrease</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;in fuel and purchased power costs.  For more information regarding FTRs, see Note 5 &#8212; &#8220;Fair Value Accounting &#8212; Derivatives and Hedging.&#8221;</font></div><a name="s0084D8A9C1C4113343FF7B9A59094BA3"></a><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:10pt;"><div style="padding-left:0px;text-indent:0px;line-height:normal;padding-top:10px;"><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;width:100%;border-collapse:collapse;text-align:left;"><tr><td colspan="5"></td></tr><tr><td width="20%"></td><td width="20%"></td><td width="20%"></td><td width="20%"></td><td width="20%"></td></tr><tr><td colspan="5" style="vertical-align:bottom;border-bottom:1px solid #000000;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;"><div style="text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Condensed Black,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:bold;">Note 4 &#8212; Jointly Owned Generation Units</font></div></td></tr></table></div></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">Cleco Power operates electric generation units that are jointly owned with other utilities.  The joint-owners are responsible for their own share of the capital and the operating and maintenance costs of the respective units. #000000;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;"><div style="text-align:right;font-size:8pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Condensed,sans-serif;font-size:8pt;">(4.88</font></div></td><td style="line-height:120%;font-size:6pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Condensed,sans-serif;font-size:6pt;"><br></font></div><div style='display:inline-block; width:100%;'><div style='float:left; width:49%;'><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">Cleco utilizes different valuation techniques for fair value calculations.  In order to measure the fair value for Level 1 assets and liabilities, Cleco obtains the closing price from published indices in active markets for the various instruments and multiplies this price by the appropriate number of instruments held.  Level 2 fair values are determined by obtaining the closing price of similar assets and liabilities from published indices in active markets and then discounted to the current period using a U.S. Treasury published interest rate as a proxy for a risk-free rate of return.   Cleco has consistently applied the Level 2 fair value technique from fiscal period to fiscal period.  Level 3 fair values are situations in which there is little, if any, market activity for the asset or liability at the measurement date and therefore estimated prices are used in the discounted cash flow approach.  </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">The assets and liabilities reported at fair value are grouped into classes based on the underlying nature and risks associated with the individual asset or liability.  </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">At </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">December&#160;31, 2013</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, Cleco and Cleco Power were exposed to concentrations of credit risk through their short-term investments classified as cash equivalents and restricted cash equivalents.  The institutional money market funds were reported on the Cleco Consolidated Balance Sheet in cash and cash equivalents, current restricted cash and cash equivalents, and non-current restricted cash and cash equivalents of </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$22.2 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$8.9 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, and </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$5.0 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, respectively, at </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">December&#160;31, 2013</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">.  At Cleco Power, the institutional money market funds were reported on the Consolidated Balance Sheet in cash and cash equivalents, current restricted cash and cash equivalents, and non-current restricted cash and cash equivalents of </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$14.9 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$8.9 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, and </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$5.0 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, respectively, at </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">December&#160;31, 2013</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">.  </font></div></div><div id='pagebreak' style='width:2%; float:left;'>&nbsp;</div><div style='float:right; width:49%;'><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">If the money market funds failed to perform under the terms of the investments, Cleco and Cleco Power would be exposed to a loss of the invested amounts.  Collateral on these types of investments is not required by either Cleco or Cleco Power. The Level 2 institutional money market funds asset consists of a single class.  In order to capture interest income and minimize risk, cash is invested in money market funds that invest primarily in short-term securities issued by the U.S. Treasury in order to maintain liquidity and achieve the goal of a net asset value of a dollar.  The risks associated with this class are counterparty risk of the fund manager and risk of price volatility associated with the underlying securities of the fund. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">The commercial paper, municipal bonds, corporate bonds, and federal agency mortgage-backed securities were reported on Cleco and Cleco Power&#8217;s Consolidated Balance Sheets in restricted investments in the amount of </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">$1.5 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">$9.8 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">,</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">$0.5 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, and </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">$1.0 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;at </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">December&#160;31, 2013</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, respectively.  The Level 2 commercial paper, the Level 2 municipal bonds, the Level 2 corporate bonds, and the Level 2 federal agency mortgage-backed securities consisted of a single class.  In order to maximize income and to meet the requirements established by the LPSC for the restricted reserve fund, restricted cash and cash equivalents were invested in short-term, fixed-income, debt instruments in order to maintain safety and liquidity.  The risks associated with this class are counterparty risk of the fund manager and risk of price volatility associated with the commercial paper, municipal bonds, corporate bonds, and federal agency mortgage-backed securities.  Quarterly, Cleco receives reports from the trustee for the investment manager which provides the fair value measurement.  Cleco performs an evaluation of those reports to verify the fair value of the securities.   </font></div></div></div><br><br><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div></div><br><div style='display:inline-block; width:100%;'><div style='float:left; width:49%;'><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">The Level 3 FTRs consisted of a single class.  As part of Cleco Power&#8217;s integration into MISO, Cleco Power was awarded FTRs in November 2013.  The FTRs were priced using MISO&#8217;s monthly estimated auction prices.  The monthly estimated auction prices are discounted to net present value to determine fair value.  FTRs are categorized as Level 3 fair value measurements because the only relevant pricing available comes from MISO auctions, which trade infrequently.  For more information about FTRs, see &#8220;&#8212; Derivatives and Hedging.&#8221; </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">The Level 2 interest rate derivative was one forward starting interest rate swap liability that consisted of a single class that only contained one instrument.  The risks were changes in the three-month LIBOR rate and counterparty risk.  This instrument was with a direct counterparty and was not traded through an exchange.  For some options, Cleco uses the Black-Scholes model using observable and available inputs to calculate the fair value, consistent with the income approach.  </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">The Level 2 long-term debt liability consists of a single class.  In order to fund capital requirements, Cleco issues long-term, fixed and variable rate debt with various tenors.  The fair value of this class fluctuates as the market interest rates for fixed and variable rate debt with similar tenors and credit ratings changes.  The fair value of the debt could also change from period to period due to changes in the credit rating of the Cleco entity that issued the debt.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">During the years ended </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">December&#160;31, 2013</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;and </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">2012</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, Cleco did not experience any transfers between levels.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Condensed Black,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Restricted Investments</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">In September 2007, the LPSC authorized the funding and securitization of a </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">$50.0 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;reserve for Cleco Power&#8217;s future storm costs.  On July 1, 2012, Cleco Power transferred </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">$13.0 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;of the related restricted cash and cash equivalents to an outside investment manager.  Investments made by the investment manager are restricted to the criteria established by management in Cleco Power&#8217;s guidelines for short-term investments.  At </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">December&#160;31, 2013</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, the investments included cash and cash equivalents and debt securities. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">The cash and cash equivalents are reflected in Cleco and Cleco Power&#8217;s Consolidated Balance Sheets at </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">December&#160;31, 2013</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, as restricted cash and cash equivalents at its approximate fair value because of its short-term nature.&#160;</font></div></div><div id='pagebreak' style='width:2%; float:left;'>&nbsp;</div><div style='float:right; width:49%;'><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">The debt securities were recorded at fair value on Cleco and Cleco Power&#8217;s Consolidated Balance Sheets at </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">December&#160;31, 2013</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, as restricted investments.  The investments in debt securities include municipal bonds, corporate bonds, federal agency mortgage-backed securities, and commercial paper with original maturity dates of more than three months and are classified as available-for-sale securities and reported at fair value.  Because Cleco Power&#8217;s investment strategy for these investments is within the requirements established by the LPSC for the restricted reserve fund, realized and unrealized gains and losses, interest income, investment management fees and custody fees are recorded directly to Cleco Power&#8217;s restricted storm reserve rather than in earnings or OCI.  As a result, no amounts will be recorded to OCI for these investments. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">Quarterly, Cleco Power&#8217;s available-for-sale debt securities are evaluated on an individual basis to determine if a decline in fair value below the carrying value is other-than-temporary.  </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">Management determines whether it intends to sell or if it is more likely than not that it will be required to sell impaired securities.  This determination considers current and forecasted liquidity and regulatory requirements.  For Cleco Power&#8217;s impaired debt securities for which there was no intent or expected requirement to sell, the evaluation assesses whether it is likely the amortized cost will be recovered considering the nature of the securities, credit rating, financial condition of the issuer, or the extent and duration of the unrealized loss and market conditions.  If Cleco Power determines that an other-than-temporary decline in value exists on its debt securities, the investments would be written down to fair value with a new basis established.  Declines in fair value below cost basis that are determined to be other-than-temporary would be recorded to Cleco Power&#8217;s restricted storm reserve.  The unrealized gains and losses on Cleco Power&#8217;s debt securities as of </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">December&#160;31, 2013</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, were caused by interest rate movements. Cleco Power does not intend to sell the debt securities and has determined it is more likely than not that it will not be required to sell the investments before recovery of the amortized cost value.  Cleco Power determined there were </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">no</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;other-than-temporary impairments on its debt securities at </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">December&#160;31, 2013</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">.     </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">At December 31, 2013 and 2012, Cleco Power had </font><font style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">As part of the integration into MISO, Cleco Power was awarded FTRs in November 2013.  FTRs provide a financial hedge to manage the risk of congestion cost in the Day-Ahead Energy Market.  FTRs represent rights to congestion credits or charges along a path during a given time frame for a certain MW quantity.  At December 31, 2013, Cleco Power had </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">6.8 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;MWh of FTRs hedged.  At December 31, 2012, Cleco Power had </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">no</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;open FTR positions.   </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Condensed Black,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">Interest Rate Derivatives</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">In November 2011, Cleco Power entered into a pay fixed/receive variable forward starting interest rate swap contract in order to mitigate the interest rate exposure on coupon payments related to the remaining </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">$50.0 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;fixed-rate forecasted debt issuance.  The forward starting interest rate swap had a spot </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">30</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">-year all-in swap rate of </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">3.05%</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, notional amount of </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">$50.0 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, with the pricing date of May 14, 2013, or the issuance of the notes, whichever was earlier.  The forward starting interest rate swap met the criteria of a cash </font></div></div><div id='pagebreak' style='width:2%; float:left;'>&nbsp;</div><div style='float:right; width:49%;'><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">flow hedge under the authoritative guidance as it related to derivatives and hedging and was carried on the balance sheet at its fair value.  Because of the inputs and common techniques used to calculate fair value, the swap valuation was considered Level 2.  </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">During the first quarter of 2013, Cleco determined that the forward starting interest rate swap ceased to be highly effective in offsetting changes in the cash flows of the forecasted coupon payments and discontinued hedge accounting prospectively.  In May 2013, upon pricing of the 2008 Series B GO Zone bonds, Cleco Power settled the forward starting interest rate swap at a loss of </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">$3.3 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">.  Of this amount, Cleco Power deferred </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">$2.9 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;as a regulatory asset and recognized </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">$0.4 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;in OCI.  In May 2013, Cleco Power began amortizing these losses over the </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">25</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">-year term of the related debt.  For more information about the 2008 Series B GO Zone bonds, see Note 6 &#8212; &#8220;Debt.&#8221;   </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">The following table presents the effect of derivatives designated as hedging instruments on Cleco and Cleco Power&#8217;s Consolidated Statements of Income for the years ended </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">December&#160;31, 2013</font><font The 2008 Series B GO Zone bonds mature on December 1, 2038.  The proceeds were used to partially fund the maturity of Cleco Power's $75.0 million 5.375% senior notes on May 1, 2013. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Condensed Black,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Interest Rate Derivatives</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:18px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Condensed Black,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:bold;">Forward Starting Interest Rate Swap</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">In November 2011, Cleco Power entered into a pay fixed/receive variable forward starting interest rate swap contract in order to mitigate the interest rate exposure on coupon payments related to a forecasted debt issuance.  The forward starting interest rate swap had a spot </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">30</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">-year all-in swap rate of </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">3.05%</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, notional amount of </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">$50.0 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, with the pricing date of May 14, 2013, or the issuance of the notes, whichever was earlier.  The forward starting interest rate swap met the criteria of a cash flow hedge under the authoritative guidance as it related to derivatives and hedging and was carried on the balance sheet at its fair value.  </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">During the first quarter of 2013, Cleco determined that the forward starting interest rate swap ceased to be highly effective in offsetting changes in the cash flows of the forecasted coupon payments and discontinued hedge accounting prospectively.  In May 2013, upon pricing of the 2008 Series B GO Zone bonds, Cleco Power settled the forward starting interest rate swap at a loss of $</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">3.3 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">.  Of this amount, Cleco Power deferred </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">$2.9 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;as a regulatory asset and recognized </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">$0.4 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;in other comprehensive income.  In May 2013, Cleco Power began amortizing these losses over the </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">25</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">-year term of the related debt.  </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Condensed Black,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Credit Facilities</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">At </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">December&#160;31, 2013</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, Cleco had two separate revolving credit facilities, one for Cleco Corporation and one for Cleco Power, with a maximum aggregate capacity of </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$550.0 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">In </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">October 2013</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, Cleco Corporation entered into a new, amended and restated </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$250.0 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;revolving credit facility.  The credit facility is set to mature on </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">October&#160;16, 2018</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;and provides for working capital and other needs.  In connection with the new credit facility, </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">$1.0 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;of unamortized debt expense related to Cleco Corporation&#8217;s previous credit facility was written off.  At December 31, 2013, the all-in interest rate under the new facility was equal to LIBOR plus </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">1.275%</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;or ABR, plus facility fees of </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">0.225%</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">.  Due to the credit ratings upgrade on January 30, 2014, the all-in interest rate under the new facility is equal to LIBOR plus </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">1.075%</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;or ABR, plus facility fees of </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">0.175%</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">.  At </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">December&#160;31, 2013</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, Cleco Corporation had </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">$5.0 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;borrowings outstanding under its existing credit facility at an all-in interest rate of </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">1.445%</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, leaving an available borrowing capacity of </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$245.0 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">. style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Condensed Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Employee Stock Purchase Plan</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">Regular, full-time, and part-time employees of Cleco Corporation and its participating subsidiaries, except officers, general managers, and employees who own </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">5%</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;or more of Cleco Corporation&#8217;s stock, may participate in the ESPP.  An eligible employee elects to participate in the ESPP by entering into an option agreement with Cleco Corporation or its affiliate authorizing payroll deductions to purchase stock at a discounted rate.  The amount of payroll deductions required by the plan are to be no less than </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$10</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;but no more than </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$350</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;each pay period.  The payroll deductions are accumulated during a calendar quarter, which is referred to as the &#8220;offering period,&#8221; and remain as general assets of Cleco pending the purchase of common stock by the plan administrator.  No trust or other fiduciary account has been established in connection with the ESPP.  At the end of each offering period, payroll deductions are automatically applied to the purchase of common stock.  Shares of common stock are purchased at a </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">5%</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;discount of the fair market value as of the last trading day of each offering period.  The number of shares of common stock purchased is determined by dividing each participant's payroll deductions during the offering period by the option price of a share of common stock.  A participant may purchase a maximum of </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">62</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;shares per offering period.  Dividends received on shares are automatically reinvested as required by the dividend reinvestment plan (DRIP) provisions of the ESPP.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">A maximum of </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">734,000</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;shares of common stock may be purchased under the ESPP, subject to adjustment for changes in the capitalization of Cleco Corporation.  The Compensation Committee of Cleco Corporation's Board of Directors monitors the ESPP. At </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">December&#160;31, 2013</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">37,401</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;shares of non-vested Cleco Corporation common stock remained outstanding under the 2000 LTICP. Under this plan, a maximum of </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">2,250,000</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;shares of Cleco Corporation common stock can be granted or awarded.  At </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">December&#160;31, 2013</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, there were </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">1,448,013</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;shares available for future grants or awards under the 2010 LTICP.  Although equity instruments awarded in the past to employees and directors have come from issuing new shares of common stock, future awards may come from purchasing outstanding shares of common stock through Cleco Corporation's common stock repurchase program.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Condensed Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">Stock Options</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">Stock options are granted at an exercise price calculated by averaging the high and low stock price on the grant date rounded to the nearest one-eighth.  Stock options granted to directors are immediately exercisable and expire after 10 years.  Stock options granted to officers and employees vest one-third each year beginning on the third anniversary of the grant date and expire after 10 years.  There were </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">no</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;stock options granted during the years ended December 31, </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">2013</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">2012</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, or </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">2011</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">. Cash received from options exercised under all stock-based compensation plans for the years ended December 31, </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">2012</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;and </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">2011</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;was </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$2.0 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;and </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$0.9 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, respectively.  The associated tax benefit for options exercised for years ended December 31, </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">2012</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;and </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">2011</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;was </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$0.7 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;and </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$0.2 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, respectively.  No cash was paid to settle equity instruments granted under the stock-based compensation plans for the years ended December 31, </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">2012</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;or </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">2011</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Condensed Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">Non-Vested Stock and Common Stock Equivalent Units</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">In </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">2013</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">2012</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, and </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">2011</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, Cleco granted non-vested stock to certain officers, key employees, and directors  Because it can only be settled in shares of Cleco Corporation common stock, non-vested stock is classified as equity.  Recipients of non-vested stock have full voting rights of a stockholder.  At the time restrictions lapse, the accrued dividend equivalent units that are paid to the recipient are prorated based upon the percentage of vested stock to the total restricted stock awarded.  </font></div></div><div id='pagebreak' style='width:2%; float:left;'>&nbsp;</div><div style='float:right; width:49%;'><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">In order to vest, the non-vested stock requires the satisfaction of a service requirement and a market-based requirement.  Recipients of non-vested stock are eligible to receive opportunity instruments if certain market-based measures are exceeded.  Cleco also awards non-vested stock with only a service period requirement to employees and directors.  These awards require the satisfaction of a pre-determined service period in order for the shares to vest.  </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">During </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">2013</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, Cleco granted </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">139,048</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;shares of non-vested stock to certain officers, key employees, and directors of Cleco pursuant to the LTICP. At December 31, </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">2013</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, the number of shares of non-vested stock previously granted with only a service period requirement for which the period had not ended was </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">119,775</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">.  </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">Under the 2010 LTICP plan, common stock equivalent units are also available to be awarded.  Because they are settled in cash, awarded common stock equivalent units are classified as a liability.  Recipients of common stock equivalent units receive dividend equivalent units under the same terms as the dividends paid on non-vested stock.  Also like non-vested stock, common stock equivalent units require the satisfaction of a service requirement and a market-based requirement.  Recipients of common stock equivalent units are eligible to receive opportunity instruments if certain market-based measures are exceeded.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">During January 2013, restrictions on all previously awarded common stock equivalent units had lapsed. Cleco has recognized stock-based compensation expense for these provisions in accordance with the non-substantive vesting period approach.  </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">Cleco recorded compensation expense for all non-vested options and non-vested stock during the years ended December 31, </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">2013</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">2012</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">, and </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">2011</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">.  Assuming achievement </font></div></div><div id='pagebreak' style='width:2%; float:left;'>&nbsp;</div><div style='float:right; width:49%;'><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">of vesting requirements is probable, stock-based compensation expense of non-vested stock is recorded during the service periods, which are generally three years, after which the restrictions lapse.  All stock-based compensation cost is measured at the grant date based on the fair value of the award and is recognized as an expense in the income statement over the award's requisite service period.  Awards that vest pro rata during the requisite service period that contain only a service condition are defined as having a graded vesting schedule and could be treated as multiple awards with separate vesting schedules.  However, Cleco has elected to treat grants with graded vesting schedules as one award and recognize the related compensation expense on a straight-line basis over the requisite service period.  </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">The ESPP does not contain optionality features beyond those listed by the authoritative guidance on stock-based compensation.  Therefore, Cleco is not required to recognize a fair-value expense related to the ESPP. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-indent:24px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">Pre-tax compensation expense reported by Cleco and Cleco Power relating to their share-based compensation plans is shown in the following Black,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">SERP</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">Certain Cleco officers are covered by the SERP.  The SERP is a non-qualified, non-contributory, defined benefit pension plan.&#160;&#160;Benefits under the plan reflect an employee&#8217;s years of service, age at retirement, and the sum of the highest base salary paid out of the last five calendar years and the average of the three highest bonuses paid during the 60 months prior to retirement, reduced by benefits received from any other defined benefit pension plan, SERP Plan, or Cleco contributions under the enhanced 401(k) Plan to the extent such contributions exceed the limits of the 401(k) Plan.&#160;&#160;Cleco does not fund the SERP liability, but instead pays for current benefits out of the general funds available.  Cleco Power has formed a Rabbi Trust designated as the beneficiary for life insurance policies issued on the SERP participants.  Proceeds from the life insurance policies are expected to be used to pay the SERP participants&#8217; life insurance benefits, as well as future SERP payments.  However, because the SERP is a non-qualified plan, the assets of the trust could be used to satisfy general creditors of Cleco Power in the event of insolvency.  All SERP benefits are paid out of the general cash available of the respective companies from which the officer retired.  </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">No</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;</font></div></div><div id='pagebreak' style='width:2%; float:left;'>&nbsp;</div><div style='float:right; width:49%;'><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">contributions to the SERP were made during the three-year period ended </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">December&#160;31, 2013</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">.  Cleco Power is considered the plan sponsor, and Support Group is considered the plan administrator.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:9pt;"><font float:left;'>&nbsp;</div><div style='float:right; width:49%;'><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:10pt;"><div style="padding-left:0px;text-indent:0px;line-height:normal;padding-top:10px;"><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;width:100%;border-collapse:collapse;text-align:left;"><tr><td colspan="5"></td></tr><tr><td width="20%"></td><td width="20%"></td><td width="20%"></td><td width="20%"></td><td width="20%"></td></tr><tr><td colspan="5" style="vertical-align:bottom;border-bottom:1px solid #000000;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;"><div style="text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Condensed Black,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:bold;">Note 14 &#8212; Litigation, Other Commitments and Contingencies, and Disclosures about Guarantees</font></div></td></tr></table></div></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Condensed Black,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Litigation</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Condensed Black,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:bold;">Devil&#8217;s Swamp</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">In October 2007, Cleco received a Special Notice for Remedial Investigation and Feasibility Study (RI/FS) from the EPA pursuant to CERCLA (also known as the Superfund statute).  CERCLA establishes several classes of PRPs for a contaminated site, and imposes strict, joint, and several liability on those PRPs for the cost of response to the contamination.  The special notice requested that Cleco Corporation and Cleco Power, along with many other listed PRPs, enter into negotiations with the EPA for the performance of an RI/FS at an area known as the Devil&#8217;s Swamp Lake site just northwest of Baton Rouge, Louisiana.  The EPA identified Cleco as one of many companies that was sending PCB wastes for disposal to the site.  The Devil&#8217;s Swamp Lake site has been proposed to be added to the National Priorities List based on the release of PCBs to fisheries and wetlands located on the site, but no final determination has been made.  The PRPs began discussing a potential proposal to the EPA in February 2008.  The EPA issued a Unilateral Administrative Order to PRP&#8217;s Clean Harbors, Inc. and Baton Rouge Disposal to Conduct an RI/FS on December 3, 2009.  The Tier 1 part of the study was complete in June 2012.  Field activities for the Tier 2 investigation were completed in July 2012.  Currently, the study/remedy selection task continues, and there is no record of a decision.  Therefore, management is unable to determine how significant Cleco&#8217;s share of the costs associated with the RI/FS and possible response action at the facility site, if any, may be and whether or not this will have a material adverse effect on the Registrants&#8217; financial condition, results of operations, or cash flows.&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Condensed Black,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:bold;">Discrimination Complaints</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">In December 2009, a complaint was filed in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Louisiana (the Court) on behalf of </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">eight</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;current employees and </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">four</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;former employees alleging that Cleco discriminated against each of them on the basis of race.  Each was seeking various remedies provided under applicable statutes prohibiting racial discrimination in the workplace, and together, the plaintiffs sought monetary compensation exceeding </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$35.0 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">.  In July 2010, the plaintiffs moved to add an additional current employee alleging that Cleco had discriminated on the basis of race.  The additional plaintiff sought compensation of no less than </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$2.5 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;and became the thirteenth plaintiff.  In April 2011, Cleco entered into a settlement with one of the current employees which resulted in a dismissal of </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">one</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;of the </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">thirteen</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;cases with prejudice.  In September 2011, the Court ruled on Cleco&#8217;s summary judgment motions, with the end result that </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">eleven</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;of the </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">twelve</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;remaining plaintiffs had at least </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">one</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;claim remaining.  In February 2013, the Court ruled on the second motion for summary judgment, filed by Cleco in March 2012, in each of the </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">eleven</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;cases and each such case was dismissed with prejudice.  Appeals were filed in </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">ten</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;of the </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">eleven</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;dismissed cases to the United States Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit (the Fifth Circuit).  In June 2013, the Fifth Circuit clerk dismissed the appeals of </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">two</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;of the current employees due to their failure to file a brief in support of their respective appeals.  On various dates in August through November 2013, </font></div></div></div><br><br><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:8pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:8pt;">105</font></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><div style="vertical-align:bottom;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;"><div style="text-align:left;font-size:7pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Condensed seven of the eight remaining cases.  There has been no disposition of the </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">one</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;remaining appeal.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">In July 2012, </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">nine</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;plaintiffs in the pending discrimination suits described above filed a new lawsuit in the same federal court in Shreveport alleging that Cleco and its Chief Executive Officer retaliated against them for pursuing their discrimination claims by directly writing them an offer of settlement that contained allegedly intimidating threats.  The nine plaintiffs consisted of </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">six</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;current employees and </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">three</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;former employees.  The plaintiffs filed an amended complaint in August 2012, stating that such settlement letters were delivered to legal counsel for each of the plaintiffs and not directly to the plaintiffs.  In September 2012, Cleco filed a motion to dismiss the lawsuit.  In November 2012, the U.S. Magistrate recommended that Cleco&#8217;s motion be granted and that the lawsuit be dismissed with prejudice.  On January 23, 2013, the motion to dismiss was granted and the retaliation claims were dismissed with prejudice.  This case was not appealed and the dismissal is now final.  </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Condensed Black,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:bold;">City of Opelousas</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">In March 2010, a complaint was filed in the 27th Judicial District Court of St. Landry Parish, State of Louisiana, on behalf of </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">three</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;Cleco Power customers in Opelousas, Louisiana.&#160;&#160;The complaint alleges that Cleco Power overcharged the plaintiffs by applying to customers in Opelousas the same retail rates as Cleco Power applies to all of its retail customers.&#160;&#160;The plaintiffs claim that Cleco Power owes customers in Opelousas more than </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$30.0 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;as a result of the alleged overcharges.  The plaintiffs allege that Cleco Power should have established, solely for customers in Opelousas, retail rates that are separate and distinct from the retail rates that apply to other customers of Cleco Power and that Cleco Power should not collect from customers in Opelousas the storm surcharge approved by the LPSC following Hurricanes Katrina and Rita.  In April 2010, Cleco Power filed a petition with the LPSC appealing to its expertise in declaring that the ratepayers of Opelousas have been properly charged the rates that are applicable to Cleco Power&#8217;s retail customers and that no overcharges have been collected.  </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:24px;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">In May 2010, a second class action lawsuit was filed in the 27th Judicial District Court of St. Landry Parish, State of Louisiana, repeating the allegations of the first complaint, which was submitted on behalf of </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">249</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;Opelousas residents.  In January 2011, the presiding judge in the state court proceeding ruled that the jurisdiction to hear the </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">two</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;class actions resides in the state court and not with the LPSC as argued by both Cleco and the LPSC Staff.  Both Cleco and the LPSC Staff appealed this ruling to the Third Circuit Court of Appeals for the State of Louisiana (Third Circuit).  In September 2011, the Third Circuit denied both appeals.  In October 2011, both Cleco and the LPSC appealed the Third Circuit&#8217;s ruling to the Louisiana Supreme Court.  In February 2011, the administrative law judge (ALJ) in the LPSC proceeding ruled that the LPSC has jurisdiction to decide the claims raised by the class action plaintiffs.  At its December 2011 Business and Executive session, the LPSC adopted the ALJ&#8217;s recommendation that Cleco be granted summary judgment in its declaratory action finding that Cleco&#8217;s ratepayers in the City of Opelousas have been served under applicable rates and policies approved by the LPSC and Cleco&#8217;s Opelousas ratepayers have not been overcharged in connection with LPSC rates or ratemaking.  In January 2012, </font></div></div><div id='pagebreak' style='width:2%; float:left;'>&nbsp;</div><div style='float:right; width:49%;'><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">the class action plaintiffs filed their appeal of such LPSC decision to the 19th Judicial District Court for East Baton Rouge Parish, State of Louisiana.  In December 2012, the Louisiana Supreme Court issued its opinion accepting Cleco&#8217;s jurisdictional arguments and dismissed the state court claims.  The only matter remaining is before the 19th Judicial District Court to review the LPSC ruling in Cleco&#8217;s favor that it had properly charged the ratepayers of Opelousas.  In view of the uncertainty of the claims, management is not able to predict or give a reasonable estimate of the possible range of liability, if any, of these claims.  However, if it is found that Cleco Power overcharged customers resulting in a refund, any such refund could have a material adverse effect on the Registrants&#8217; results of operations, financial condition, and cash flows.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Condensed Black,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:bold;">LPSC Audits</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Condensed Black,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Condensed Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Fuel Audit</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">The cost of fuel used for electric generation and the cost of power purchased for utility customers are recovered through the LPSC-established FAC, which enables Cleco Power to pass on to its customers substantially all such charges.  The LPSC FAC General Order issued November 6, 1997, in Docket No. U-21497 provides that an audit of FAC filings will be performed at least every other year.  In March 2009, the LPSC initiated an audit of FAC filings for the years 2003 through 2008.  The total amount of fuel expenses included in the audit was approximately </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$3.26 billion</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">.  In February 2012, the LPSC Staff&#8217;s consultant issued an audit report recommending a cost disallowance of approximately </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$0.4 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;plus interest for these filing years.  The report was approved by the LPSC on July 18, 2012.  Cleco Power made refunds of </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$0.4 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;plus interest to customers during the September 2012 billing cycle.  Cleco Power has FAC filings for the years 2009 through 2013 that remain subject to audit.    </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Condensed Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Condensed Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Environmental Audit</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">In July 2009, the LPSC issued Docket No. U-29380 Subdocket A, which provides for an EAC to recover certain costs of environmental compliance as an additional charge on customers&#8217; bills.  The costs eligible for recovery are prudently incurred air emissions credits associated with complying with federal, state, and local air emission regulations that apply to the generation of electricity reduced by the sale of such allowances.  Also eligible for recovery are variable emission mitigation costs, which are the costs of reagents such as ammonia and limestone that are a part of the fuel mix used to, among other things, reduce air emissions.  Cleco Power anticipates incurring environmental compliance expenses beginning in the second quarter of 2015 for additional reagents associated with compliance with MATS.  These expenses would be eligible for recovery through Cleco Power's EAC and subject to review by the LPSC.  In November 2011, the LPSC opened Docket No. X-32150 to audit the costs for the periods October 2009 through October 2010.  The total amount of environmental expenses included in the audit was approximately</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#32;</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">$11.3 million</font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">.  </font><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">In April 2012, the LPSC Staff&#8217;s consultant issued an audit report recommending no cost disallowance for the review period.  There was no opposition from intervenors to the recommendations of the LPSC Staff&#8217;s consultant and the report was approved by the LPSC in July 2012.  Cleco Power has EAC filings for the years 2010 through 2013 that remain subject to audit.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica Light,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</font></div></div></div><br><br><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:8pt;"><font style="font-family:Helvetica
